checks: The same-batch full-size theorem gives δ_0>0, a unique q in int C and every old cap margin at q equal to δ_0.
Since n≥1, arbitrarily small base displacements outside the integer lattice exist. Choose q' interior with every old margin still positive.
The normal map sends D={a_i·v≤1} bijectively to the standard simplex via the weighted normalized deficits. Full rank and balance make the image sum-one and give boundedness and nonempty interior.
The lattice cylinder is closed and q' has positive distance to it and to the exterior of int C. A sufficiently small h makes q'+hD satisfy both restrictions.

New thresholds a_i·q'+h exceed the old thresholds, so cap nesting gives strict mixed budgets directly, even for vertical normals and atom-bearing thresholds. This is a stronger justification of the budget step than the continuity proviso in the final paragraph of f8f6582d5c261f3e §1.

dependencies.hypotheses: The invoked case has k=N+1 proper closed caps, strictly exclusive witnesses in C and an empty closed complementary system. Rank N and the unique first contact with positive common old margin are the exact predecessor outputs.

overlap.comparison: Provides a strict-budget open covering menu on the mixed trace under different hypotheses. It gives neither an interior first real contact nor the small full-dimensional complementary simplex.

readability: The base displacement changes the contact position first, then h raises all complementary thresholds uniformly around that position.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen candidate, with original-source, dependency and scope checks.
summary: Translating the unique full-rank contact slightly in base coordinates and scaling its complementary simplex gives the desired interior lattice-free polytope, with each cap nested in the original cap.
